source.title: Proposal: Sourcing CRM v1 — suppliers, contacts, interactions, samples, follow-ups

labels.name: proposal
labels.description: Feature proposal from the agent — awaiting Z's decision

labels.name: agent
labels.description: Opened or worked by the autonomous agent

source.body:
**Decision needed:** approve building the first slice of a sourcing CRM. **Recommendation: approve.** This is the shared core for every segment, and no competitor offers it to buyers or brokers.

## Problem / opportunity
Your core jobs include finding and vetting suppliers, CRM, and follow-ups. Today the app knows markets but nothing about *your* relationships. Competitors split the job up: marketplaces show only their own listings, Cropster Origin's CRM is producer-side, and CropConex/greensquare are trader catalogues. greensquare's survey found roasters juggling 6–8 traders in different formats. Nobody gives a buyer or broker one neutral view of every counterparty.

## Proposed feature (what Z will see and be able to do)
- A new **Sourcing** tab with a searchable list of **organisations** (producer/farm, micro-mill, co-op, exporter, importer, roaster/buyer). Each has its origin and region (Costa Rica regions pre-filled from config), contact people, and free-text notes.
- On each organisation: a log of **interactions** (visit, call, WhatsApp, email, plus date and summary), **samples** (lot name, process, variety, received date, status: requested → received → cupped → approved/rejected), and **follow-ups** with due dates.
- A "Due soon" strip on the Sourcing tab showing overdue and upcoming follow-ups.
- CSV export of everything (your data is portable).

## Approach (files touched, data sources + their terms, new dependencies)
- `app/store.py`: new `crm_*` tables in SQLite (local) and collections in Firestore (cloud), behind the existing storage interface.
- `app/main.py`: REST endpoints `/api/crm/orgs`, `/api/crm/orgs/{id}`, `/interactions`, `/samples`, `/followups`, `/api/crm/export.csv`.
- `app/static/app.js` + `app.css`: Sourcing tab, mobile-first layout.
- `app/demo/fixtures.py`: a handful of clearly fictional demo records, so demo mode works offline.
- Tests: CRUD and export tests in `tests/test_crm.py`.
- No new data sources and no new dependencies.
- Rejected alternative: a Google Sheets–backed CRM. It's quicker, but it adds an account and API dependency, works badly offline, and doesn't scale to teams.

## Out of scope
Multi-user/permissions (designed for later via an owner field), offline sync (see the field-mode proposal), cupping scores (field-mode proposal), email/WhatsApp integration, file uploads.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Create, edit and delete orgs, contacts, interactions, samples and follow-ups in demo and live mode
- [ ] Overdue follow-ups are highlighted; search by name, origin and type
- [ ] CSV export round-trips all fields
- [ ] Usable at 375 px phone width
- [ ] ruff + pytest pass; demo-mode curl smoke test of the new endpoints

## Size: M (2–3 runs)
Run 1: data model, API and tests. Run 2: UI. Run 3: export and polish.

## Research behind it
[agent/research/2026-10-15-competitor-landscape.md](https://github.com/zack-hum/coffee-intelligence-v1.1/blob/docs/research-2026-10-15/agent/research/2026-10-15-competitor-landscape.md)

**How we'll know it worked:** you log every Costa Rica contact in it during the trip instead of in your notes app.
